subject: F4149E168A75E0609E7D38FC1193D523
introduction: These are prayers of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá and Bahá’u’lláh for people in want: merchants whose trade has failed, families impoverished by persecution, believers who gave what they had. They ask plainly for livelihood and ease, and almost always in the same breath for “true riches”, contentment and the good of the next world. The Lord’s Prayer asks for daily bread; the third epistle of John wishes a friend prosperity “even as thy soul prospereth”; Paul has learned both to be abased and to abound. Agur’s “neither poverty nor riches” and Paul’s warning about the love of money are the limits scripture sets on such prayer.
questions: Is it right to pray for prosperity? What do these prayers add to the request that keeps it from being greed?
What do the prayers mean by “true riches”?
Agur asks for neither poverty nor riches. Would you pray that prayer?

outside.why: His patience is exhausted from hardship. How long shall I take counsel in my soul, having sorrow in my heart daily?
Businesses shaken and earnings diminished. Give us this day our daily bread.
Poor, grant us a share from the ocean of Thy wealth. The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.
These bitter days shall pass. Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
Make these poor ones wealthy and these oppressed ones honoured. Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth.
Make every needy one wealthy. Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin.
Grant him means, and true riches from Thy celestial treasury. The blessing of the Lord, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it.

Agur’s prayer asked for less: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: lest I be full, and deny thee. Is it right to pray for wealth, as these prayers do, and what does Agur fear that they do not?
Enricher of the poor, Provider for the weak. I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content: I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound.
Servants who have spent their wealth in Thy path. Prove me now herewith, if I will not open you the windows of heaven.
Ordain for me the good of this world and the next. Seek ye first the kingdom of God; and all these things shall be added unto you.
Prayers for provision. The love of money is the root of all evil. How does a person pray for means without coming to love them?

shortfall: The sixty prayers ask for provision and for “the good of this world and the next” in nearly the same words; a companion was given to each distinct petition among the first dozen.
